text: Dynamic Data Masking changes what a column looks like. Row-Level Security restricts which rows a query is even allowed to see, based on a predicate matching the user's identity against a value in the row.
Two sales reps run the exact same SELECT * FROM Orders, with identical table-level permissions. Each sees only their own rows — the security policy filters below the object-permission layer entirely.
A predicate function checks the current session against a column value. A security policy binds that function to a table as a filter or block predicate — this is what actually does the restricting.
A FILTER predicate silently narrows what SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE return. A BLOCK predicate actively rejects a write that would violate the rule, throwing an error instead.

RLS needs zero application code changes, which is powerful and risky if you forget it's there — missing rows might be RLS working correctly. Next up: Data Discovery and Classification, finding which columns need this in the first place.
